newsitem.title: INDIA: Kashmir's new chief minister calls for investment.
newsitem.headline: Kashmir's new chief minister calls for investment.

text.p: The new chief minister of India's troubled Jammu-Kashmir state invited foreign investors on Monday to help fuel an economic recovery in the Himalayan region after six years of separatist violence.

Farooq Abdullah, whose pro-India National Conference party won control of the state assembly in Kashmir's first local elections in nine years in September, told an economic conference in New Delhi he welcomed investments in power, tourism, forestry and food processing.
"You make the investments and bring the technology. We would provide you with infrastructure," he told the international gathering organised by the Swiss-based World Economic Forum.
"In the tourism sector, we would need a large number of people to come in," Abdullah said.
He urged investors to fund development of ski slopes, hotels, and new tourist sites in the state.
"I am meeting the prime minister (H.D. Deve Gowda) today and I hope to get... industries back on their feet," Abdullah said.
He said Kashmir's Chenab River was able to support hydroelectric projects to meet growing power needs in neighbouring Punjab, Haryana, Delhi and Rajasthan states.
"We could generate enough power in the state for these states," Abdullah said.
Abdullah also said the state wanted to adopt forestry measures similar to Sweden's.
September's polls were aimed at returning democracy to the state after six years of direct rule by India, imposed in 1990 after Muslim separatists launched a revolt.

Two of the three wars Pakistan and India have fought since their independence in 1947 have been over Jammu-Kashmir. Pakistan denies frequent Indian charges that it arms the separatists, saying it provides only diplomatic support.
Abdullan was chief minister in 1990 when New Delhi imposed direct rule.
More than 20,000 people have died in violence in the state, the only one with a Moslem majority in predominantly Hindu India.
